newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN FLOWER IMPORTER SEEKS TO BEAT KENYAN GENERAL.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN FLOWER IMPORTER SEEKS TO BEAT KENYAN GENERAL.

text.p: The leading German importer of Kenyan flowers said it was seeking to re-route Europe-bound air cargo shipments to beat a likely general strike on Friday.
Juergen Riebel, sales manager of Kenya Flowers GmbH, said the import company was seeking ways to fly flowers from Nairobi into Amsterdam instead of to Germany on Friday.

He was speaking after Lufthansa Cargo said it expected to cancel its Friday Boeing 747 freighter flight from Nairobi to Frankfurt amid serious concerns over safety caused by the go-slow strike by Kenyan air traffic controllers.

The Kenyan opposition has called a general strike for Friday which is expected to impact severely on operations at Nairobi airport. Riebel told Reuters: " The go-slow has not had a big impact yet and we are waiting to see what happens. But we are trying to fly out a lot of flowers before Friday.
" The likely solution would be to fly the shipments to Amsterdam where the importer had a subsidiary company or to another European airport" he said.

Kenya Flowers, based in the Kelsterbach air cargo village at Frankfurt airport and part of the Florimex group, normally imported into Germany and then distributed Europe-wide, he added. Riebel declined to disclose the size of the company's flower imports from Kenya but described the firm as the market leader.
